notes: SHIP v1.14.457 - THE CONTEXT ENGINE (SHIP-CONTEXT-INJECT-369 V3, RESCOPED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-13). THE SPEC DESCRIBED BUILDING WHAT ALREADY EXISTED, and that is the first thing to record. Its section 1 specified a SiteProfile module on key phantom_site_profile_v1. That key has been live at 24091 since the SITE-PROFILE workstream, on a V2 schema behind siteProfile_migrateV1toV2, with load, save, reset, a prompt block builder and a settings editor - so implementing section 1 literally would have built a duplicate store AND regressed the schema, since the spec asks for schemaVersion 1. Its section 6 asked for AI call sites to be wired to a single choke point; activeContext_getContextBlock has BEEN that choke point and its own comment at 27665 says so, with seven call sites already routed through it. Owner ruled execute the intent against live code and report the deviation. This ship therefore WRAPS the existing door rather than building a second one - Contract A2, and the .431 lesson about searching for a spec's NAME instead of its concept. WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW. buildContext is the single entry every AI call now uses. It always emits an honesty guard header that can never be dropped, then the existing site and deployment block, then a JobState snapshot, then a deterministic MASTER slice, then caller extra - under a roughly 2200 token ceiling with truncation ONLY at line boundaries and an explicit [+N more records omitted] marker, because a prompt cut mid-record hands the model half a fact that reads as complete. Drop order is MASTER detail, then extra, then JobState; the site block and the guard are never dropped. AI_PERMISSION is READ and assertAIPermission runs at the choke point; SUGGEST and CHANGE both throw, and CHANGE has no implementation path anywhere. WHAT JobState DELIBERATELY DOES NOT EMIT. The existing block already states SITE, DEPLOYMENT and ACTIVE RACK. Re-emitting them would put two copies of one truth into a single prompt, and when they drifted the model would have no way to choose which to believe. JobState adds only PHASE, OPEN ISSUES / BLOCKERS, AUDITS RECORDED, LAST SCAN, MANIFEST and OPERATOR. THREE HONESTY DECISIONS INSIDE THE FIELD SET. First, the spec asked for a BURNDOWN count; there is no burndown record. The counts are real - issues, discrepancies and open blockers - but naming them after a surface rather than after the records they come from binds a panel to a NAME instead of to the truth, so the owner ruled the label is OPEN ISSUES / BLOCKERS. Second, the spec asked for AUDIT warnings; no warning count is computed anywhere, so emitting one would be inventing a figure, and the field is relabelled AUDITS RECORDED which is a real fact. Third, MANIFEST is degraded to a presence flag on purpose, because phantom_manifest_last_deploy holds a deployment id string and nothing else. BOM match percent and PORT MAP were EXCLUDED outright for having no backing source, per the spec's own rule that unsourced fields are excluded rather than stubbed. THE PLACEHOLDER TRAP THIS SHIP AVOIDS, worth recording. PHANTOM_PHASE_MODEL seeds every step with the label PHASE - step not yet defined for this site, because real per-platform commissioning procedure is site knowledge the app does not have. Feeding those labels to a model as if they were procedure is fabricated telemetry wearing a checklist, so PHASE emits STATE ONLY - counts and the in-progress phase name - and spec 38 pins that the placeholder string can never reach either the snapshot or the prompt. OPERATOR resolves through identity_getUser, never through phantom_current_user_v1 directly: 24106 records that the raw key was a SECOND persisted answer to who is working and was demoted to a migration fallback, so reading it here would resurrect a split-brain that .418 deleted. Contract 9a - the ACTOR is credited. CONTEXT PREVIEW ships in the profile editor: a read-only render of the exact text buildContext hands the model, built by CALLING buildContext rather than describing it, because a preview built from a second code path would eventually disagree with what actually ships. Its zero state SAYS there is no context yet instead of rendering an empty box. THE CALLER PROMPTS WERE NOT ROUTED THROUGH extra, and this is a deliberate deviation. Each of the seven call sites concatenates its whole feature system prompt after the context block. extra is capped at 500 tokens, so passing those prompts through it would have silently truncated the instructions that make each feature work. The roughly 2200 cap governs the context ENGINE's output; the feature prompt is separate and always was. RUNS (phone-webkit, alone): spec 38 context-engine 7 passed. GATES: three-stamp lockstep at .457, inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, brace balance, 0 bare LF, 0 mojibake. DEVICE-VERIFY: open SITE PROFILE and read CONTEXT PREVIEW. PASS is every line tracing to real data, empty fields absent rather than blank, no step text reading step not yet defined, and asking an AI feature about a field you left empty gets record not available rather than an invention. FAIL is any fabricated value, a blank labelled row, or placeholder step text in the preview.
